question: What do the numbers show, and why do people behave that way?

fetters2013.cite: Fetters, Curry & Creswell (2013). Achieving integration in mixed methods designs—principles and practices. Health Services Research 48(6 Pt 2): 2134 ff.
fetters2013.checked: every quote read word for word in the PMC article page (PMC4097839) on 20 Nov 2026; the PMC page has no page numbers, so places are section headings; in-text citations (author, year) are left out where marked

steps.title: Choose the order
steps.text: Decide which phase comes first. Numbers first, then interviews to explain them; or interviews first, then a survey to test what they found.

quotes.text: In sequential designs, the intent is to have one phase of the mixed methods study build on the other

steps.title: Numbers first
steps.text: In the explanatory order, run and analyse the survey first. Its results, such as an unexpected gap, set the questions for the next phase.

quotes.text: In an explanatory sequential design, the researcher first collects and analyzes quantitative data, then the findings inform qualitative data collection and analysis
quotes.where: “Integration at the Study Design Level” (citation to Ivankova, Creswell and Stick 2006 left out)

steps.title: Connect the samples
steps.text: Choose the interviewees from the survey respondents, by what the survey found: for example, people from both sides of the gap.

quotes.text: if the baseline survey data are analyzed, and then the participants sampled based on findings from the analysis, then the design is explanatory sequential.
quotes.where: “Integration at the Methods Level”, on connecting

steps.title: Or build a survey
steps.text: In the exploratory order, the interviews come first and supply the topics and the very words of the survey items.

quotes.text: Items for inclusion in a survey are built upon previously collected qualitative data that generate hypotheses or identify constructs or language used by research participants.
quotes.where: “Integration at the Methods Level”, on building

steps.title: Integrate and check fit
steps.text: Bring both results together, for instance in one joint table, and say whether they confirm each other, add to each other, or disagree.

quotes.text: The “fit” of data integration refers to coherence of the quantitative and qualitative findings.
Discordance occurs if the qualitative and quantitative findings are inconsistent, incongruous, contradict, conflict, or disagree with each other.
